answer: Decaying anchor ledger: each identity pays a fee that decays a little every day it stays active, so idle hordes grow expensive. A new identity must first post a sinking deposit that is forfeited unless it clears a reef of independent transaction confirmations. An attacker needs one live plume of real activity per fake account to recover the deposit. Cost scales linearly: N sybils require N deposits plus N activity streams, making mass fabrication costly.
